title: Triangle compatibility of the external direct-image comparison
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X,Y,Z$ schemes over $k$, $f:X\to Y$ a $k$-morphism, $h=f\times\mathrm{id}_Z$, and $p_X,p_Z,p_Y,p'_Z$ the projections from $X\times_kZ$ and $Y\times_kZ$. Use small representatives of the small étale sites [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-etale-site], a commutative coefficient ring $A$, the module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Fix $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ represented by a bounded complex of flat sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. On $D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put
$$F(Q)=p_Y^*Rf_*L\otimes_A^Lp_Z'^*Q,\qquad G(Q)=Rh_*(p_X^*L\otimes_A^Lp_Z^*Q),$$
with values in the ambient unbounded category $D((Y\times_kZ)_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Let $\alpha_Q:F(Q)\to G(Q)$ be the exchange morphism [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] of the Cartesian square formed by $f,h,p_Y,p_X$, tensored with $p_Z'^*Q$, followed by the projection morphism $\mathrm{PF}_h(p_X^*L,p_Z'^*Q)$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and then by $Rh_*$ of $1\otimes c_Q$, where $c_Q:h^{-1}p_Z'^{-1}Q\xrightarrow{\sim}p_Z^{-1}Q$ is the termwise inverse-image composition isomorphism for $p_Z=p'_Z\circ h$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear]. With the canonical shift structures on derived inverse image, tensor and direct image, $F,G$ are triangulated functors [def-weil-triangulated-category], and $\alpha$ is natural and commutes with shifts: writing $s_F:F(Q[1])\simeq F(Q)[1]$ and $s_G:G(Q[1])\simeq G(Q)[1]$, one has $s_G\alpha_{Q[1]}=\alpha_Q[1]s_F$. For every distinguished triangle of bounded-below $Q_i$, the three $\alpha_{Q_i}$ give a morphism of the two image distinguished triangles, including their connecting square. No component of $\alpha$ is asserted to be invertible.

proof.text: Regard each small étale topos as ringed by its constant sheaf $A_T$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], for every scheme map $u$ the map $u^{-1}A_T\to A_{T'}$ is an isomorphism and module pullback is canonically the exact module inverse image. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to this exact functor: its derived functor is termwise inverse image, is triangulated, and its canonical shift is the identity on each term. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] this same functor computes $Lu^*$. Thus constant-coefficient specializations of ringed-topos derived pullbacks use exactly the inverse images and canonical shifts of the statement.

Smallness of the site supplies K-injective resolutions for every module complex by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Consequently [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], applied to the additive module direct image, makes $Rh_*$ an unbounded triangulated functor with its canonical derived shift. Tensor with any fixed derived object is triangulated in either variable by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite] to the pullbacks of Step 1, these tensor functors and $Rh_*$. It follows that $F$, $G$, and the intermediate functors $H(Q)=Rh_*E\otimes_A^L K_Q$ and $J(Q)=Rh_*(E\otimes_A^Lh^{-1}K_Q)$ are triangulated, where $E=p_X^*L$ and $K_Q=p_Z'^*Q$. Their shifts are the canonical composite shifts. Here $F,G,H,J$ may first be defined on all of $D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$; restriction to the strictly full triangulated subcategory $D^+$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] retains this property.

proof.text: Put $U=p_Y^*Rf_*L$, $V=Rh_*E$ and $e=\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,L}:U\to V$, the single morphism supplied by [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. Define $a_Q=e\otimes1_{K_Q}:F(Q)\to H(Q)$, $b_Q=\mathrm{PF}_h(E,K_Q):H(Q)\to J(Q)$, and $d_Q=Rh_*(1_E\otimes c_Q):J(Q)\to G(Q)$. The formula of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and the module composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] show that the comparison in the statement is precisely $\alpha_Q=d_Qb_Qa_Q$. This is its specified factorization, with $e$ held fixed as $Q$ varies.

source.place: Displayed exchange/projection composite immediately before Step 1; Step 2, “Both sides of the comparison are exact in Q”.

proof.text: The canonical second-input shift $t_{B,C}:B\otimes_A^L C[1]\xrightarrow{\sim}(B\otimes_A^LC)[1]$ multiplies the summand with first degree $p$ by $(-1)^p$ for the total tensor differential in [def-kun-derived-tensor]. For a degree-zero chain map $v:B\to B'$, both $t_{B',C}(v\otimes1_{C[1]})$ and $(v\otimes1_C)[1]t_{B,C}$ act on that summand by $(-1)^p(v^p\otimes1)$. This equality is preserved under composition and inversion of quasi-isomorphisms, so [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] gives it for every derived morphism $v$, in particular $v=e$. Termwise inverse image commutes with shift by Step 1. Substituting $C=K_Q$ proves $s_Ha_{Q[1]}=a_Q[1]s_F$. Bifunctoriality in the cited descent statement also proves naturality of $a$ in $Q$.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and the construction preceding it), with the signed total tensor; Tag 0G7D (lemma-factor-through-K-flat).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] to $h$, the constant sheaves of rings $A$, and the fixed object $E$. Its pullback is the exact $h^{-1}$ of Step 1. Its transformation is exactly $\mathrm{PF}_h(E,-)$: both it and [def-kun-projection-formula-map] are adjoint to $(\varepsilon_{h,E}\otimes1)\mu_{Rh_*E,-}$, with the same canonical pullback tensor comparison and derived adjunction. The cited theorem asserts naturality and shift compatibility for this map for arbitrary unbounded module complexes. Precomposing with $p_Z'^*$ and using [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker](iii) therefore gives $s_Jb_{Q[1]}=b_Q[1]s_H$, as well as naturality of $b$. No invertibility assertion for $b$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); the shift-compatible mate is the existing ringed-projection-mate-exact lemma.

proof.text: The isomorphism $c:h^{-1}p_Z'^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}p_Z^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] is natural on module sheaves. Applied termwise to a complex $C$, its component in degree $q$ is $c_{C^q}$. Hence at $C[1]$ it is $c_{C^{q+1}}$, exactly the degree-$q$ component of $c_C[1]$; naturality for the differential proves the chain-map equality. These exact inverse images descend with those same identity shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], so $c_{Q[1]}=c_Q[1]$ under the canonical comparisons. Tensoring on the left by $E$ preserves this equality: on the summand of first degree $p$ either order applies $c$ in the second factor and the scalar $(-1)^p$. The bifunctor descent in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] gives the same identity on derived objects. Postcomposing by $Rh_*$ and [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker](ii) yield $s_Gd_{Q[1]}=d_Q[1]s_J$. Naturality of $c$, tensor and $Rh_*$ gives naturality of $d$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker](i), the three natural transformations of Steps 4–6 compose to a natural shift-compatible transformation. Explicitly, $s_G\alpha_{Q[1]}=s_Gd_{Q[1]}b_{Q[1]}a_{Q[1]}=d_Q[1]s_Jb_{Q[1]}a_{Q[1]}=d_Q[1]b_Q[1]s_Ha_{Q[1]}=d_Q[1]b_Q[1]a_Q[1]s_F=\alpha_Q[1]s_F$. These are the canonical $s_F,s_G$ of Step 2, so this proves the claimed shift equation for the actual composite.

source.place: Tag 014V (definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories), paragraph defining a 2-morphism of triangulated functors; composition of compatible natural transformations.

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle $Q_1\xrightarrow{u}Q_2\xrightarrow{v}Q_3\xrightarrow{w}Q_1[1]$, its image triangles under $F,G$ are distinguished by Step 2. Naturality of $\alpha$ gives the first two squares. The connecting square is the equality $\alpha_{Q_1}[1]\,s_F\,F(w)=s_G\,\alpha_{Q_1[1]}F(w)=s_G\,G(w)\alpha_{Q_3}$, using Step 7 and naturality at $w$. This is exactly the third square in the definition of a morphism of triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Thus the three specified components give the required morphism of distinguished triangles.
